abstract:
Cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) is an essential technique for resolving high-resolution structures of macromolecular complexes in situ. However, the extremely low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) in tilt series, caused by strict electron dose limitations, remains a major bottleneck for subtomogram averaging (STA). Although existing denoising methods can enhance tomogram contrast, they may compromise the high-frequency structural information required for downstream STA refinement.
We introduce CryoET-DDM, a diffusion framework for high-fidelity restoration of cryo-ET tilt series that integrates data-driven noise modeling and fidelity-guided structural preservation. CryoET-DDM incorporates background noise patches extracted from the same experimental tilt series into the diffusion process to model the noise characteristics of low-dose imaging. A fidelity-guided learning objective promotes structural consistency during denoising, helping preserve high-frequency information needed for STA. Experiments on three public datasets (EMPIAR-10499, EMPIAR-10164, and EMPIAR-10651) show that CryoET-DDM improves particle quality, preserves structural fidelity, and yields downstream gains in STA resolution. These results support tilt series denoising as a promising strategy for cryo-ET data processing and improve the reliability of in situ structural biology analysis.
Code and models for our experiments are available at https://github.com/xinsheng44/CryoET-DDM. The real datasets used in this study are publicly available from EMPIAR.
